entities.name: Mohandas K. Gandhi
entities.intro: The narrator. Writing in 1925–29, aged mid‑50s, from his ashram at Sabarmati; the story itself starts with his birth in 1869.

entities.name: Mahadev Desai
entities.intro: Gandhi's secretary and translator of the autobiography from Gujarati into English.

entities.name: Miraben (Madeleine Slade)
entities.intro: Englishwoman who joined Gandhi's ashram in 1925 and revised the English of this translation.

entities.name: Swami Anand
entities.intro: Gandhi's coworker and manager of Navajivan who pressed him to write the autobiography.

entities.name: Jairamdas
entities.intro: Fellow prisoner at Yeravda jail who urged Gandhi to finish the autobiography.

entities.name: Uttamchand (Ota) Gandhi
entities.intro: Gandhi's grandfather, Diwan of Porbandar, remembered as a man of principle.

entities.name: Karamchand (Kaba) Gandhi
entities.intro: Gandhi's father: Diwan (Prime Minister) of Porbandar, later of Rajkot and Vankaner. Truthful, brave, generous, short‑tempered and incorruptible.

entities.name: Putlibai
entities.intro: Gandhi's mother, Karamchand's fourth wife. Deeply religious, kept hard vows and fasts; shrewd about State affairs.

entities.name: Tulsidas Gandhi (uncle)
entities.intro: Gandhi's uncle, Karamchand's younger brother, who also served as Prime Minister of Porbandar.

entities.name: Kasturbai (Kasturba) Gandhi
entities.intro: Gandhi's wife, married to him at thirteen. Illiterate at first; simple, independent, persevering, and braver than her husband.

entities.name: Laxmidas (eldest brother)
entities.intro: Gandhi's eldest brother, already married when Mohandas was a boy; the family's senior figure after the father.

entities.name: Karsandas (second brother)
entities.intro: Gandhi's second brother, two or three years older, married in the same triple wedding.

entities.name: Mr. Giles
entities.intro: Educational Inspector who visited Gandhi's high school.

entities.name: Dorabji Edulji Gimi
entities.intro: Headmaster of the Rajkot high school; a disciplinarian who made gymnastics and cricket compulsory.

entities.name: Krishnashankar Pandya
entities.intro: Gandhi's Sanskrit teacher at high school.

entities.name: The Friend (Sheikh Mehtab)
entities.intro: A schoolfriend of Gandhi's elder brother, athletic and daring. The book never names him; historians identify him as Sheikh Mehtab.

entities.name: Harishchandra & Shravana
entities.intro: Heroes of two plays Gandhi saw as a child: Harishchandra, who suffered every ordeal for truth, and Shravana, devoted son of blind parents.

entities.name: Porbandar
entities.intro: Coastal princely state in Kathiawad, Gujarat; Gandhi's birthplace (2 Oct 1869), where his father was Diwan.

entities.name: Rajkot
entities.intro: Princely state in Kathiawad where the family moved when Gandhi was about seven.

entities.name: Kathiawad
entities.intro: Peninsula in western India (Gujarat) made up of many small princely states.

entities.name: Sabarmati Ashram
entities.intro: Gandhi's ashram near Ahmedabad, from which he writes this book.

entities.name: Truth (Satya)
entities.intro: The book's governing idea: Gandhi worships God as Truth and calls his life a series of experiments with it.

entities.name: Ahimsa (nonviolence)
entities.intro: Nonviolence, or love that refuses to harm. Gandhi treats it as part of truth.

entities.name: Brahmacharya & desire
entities.intro: Self-restraint, especially sexual. Gandhi narrates his struggle with desire candidly.

entities.name: Meat, diet & vegetarianism
entities.intro: Gandhi was raised a strict Vaishnava vegetarian in a region shaped by Jainism. Food becomes a lifelong field of experiment.

entities.name: Child marriage
entities.intro: The custom by which Gandhi was married at thirteen, which he later condemns.

entities.name: Religion & faith
entities.intro: Gandhi's religious upbringing: Vaishnava Hindu, with strong Jain influence in Gujarat.

chapters.situation: Before the story starts, the translator explains how this English version came about.
chapters.summary: Mahadev Desai explains that he translated the weekly Gujarati chapters for Young India, with Gandhi revising the meaning and Miraben the English.

updates.desai: Translated the autobiography week by week from Gujarati for Young India.
updates.miraben: Revised the English of the translation; she had joined the ashram about a year and a half earlier.

chapters.situation: Gandhi, now in his fifties and famous as the 'Mahatma', sits down at his ashram to explain why he is writing his life story at all.
chapters.summary: Gandhi says this is not a true autobiography but an account of his 'experiments with truth', written weekly for Navajivan. His aim is self-realization, to see God, whom he worships as Truth. He promises to hide none of his faults.

updates.gandhi: Explains his purpose: to record his spiritual and moral experiments rather than his political fame, which pains him. Says the title 'Mahatma' has never pleased him.
updates.anand: Persuaded Gandhi to write the autobiography for Navajivan.
updates.jairamdas: Urged Gandhi in Yeravda jail to write the autobiography.
updates.truth: Gandhi defines Truth as more than honest speech: truthfulness in thought, and ultimately God. He holds to relative truth until he finds the Absolute.
updates.ahimsa: Named as one of the principles his experiments will cover, alongside celibacy.
updates.religion: Gandhi says the essence of religion is morality and that his goal is moksha, to see God face to face.

status.gandhi: Age ~56, at Sabarmati Ashram, writing the autobiography weekly

chapters.situation: The story proper begins with Gandhi's family background in the princely states of Kathiawad.
chapters.summary: Gandhi describes his family of Bania caste who became Prime Ministers: his principled grandfather Ota, his incorruptible but short-tempered father Kaba, and his saintly mother Putlibai. He is born at Porbandar on 2 October 1869, the youngest child, and is a slow pupil.

updates.gandhi: Born 2 October 1869 at Porbandar, the youngest of Putlibai's children. A sluggish pupil who struggled with multiplication tables.
updates.ota: Diwan of Porbandar until State intrigues forced him to Junagadh. He saluted the Nawab there with his left hand because his right was 'pledged to Porbandar'.
updates.karamchand: Married four times. Served as Diwan of Porbandar, Rajkot and Vankaner. Once refused to apologise to a British agent who insulted his chief, and was briefly detained for it. Left little property.
updates.putlibai: Mother of a daughter and three sons. Keeps punishing vows, such as not eating until she sees the sun in the rainy season, and is respected at court for her intelligence.
updates.tulsidas: Karamchand's younger brother and his successor as Prime Minister of Porbandar.
updates.porbandar: Gandhi's birthplace; the family served here as Diwans for generations.
updates.religion: The family are Vaishnavas. His mother's daily temple visits and vows are his first model of faith.

status.gandhi: Infant and small boy at Porbandar
status.karamchand: Diwan, member of the Rajasthanik Court

chapters.situation: Gandhi is born and spends his first years in Porbandar. His father, an honest Diwan, is about to take up a new post.
chapters.summary: At about seven Gandhi moves to Rajkot when his father joins the Rajasthanik Court. He is a shy, mediocre but honest student who refuses to copy even when his teacher prompts him. Two plays about Shravana and Harishchandra fix the ideals of devotion and truth in his mind.

updates.gandhi: A painfully shy schoolboy who runs home after class. He refuses to copy a spelling ('kettle') from a neighbour when the teacher nudges him to.
updates.giles: Set the spelling test at which Gandhi misspelt 'kettle' and refused to copy.
updates.harishchandra: The Shravana play and pictures make Gandhi want to serve his parents. The Harishchandra play makes him ask why everyone should not be truthful.
updates.rajkot: The family moves here when Gandhi is about seven; he goes through primary, suburban and high school.
updates.truth: Harishchandra becomes his childhood ideal of truth.

chapters.situation: Gandhi is a shy, truthful schoolboy in Rajkot, inspired by the plays of Harishchandra and Shravana.
chapters.summary: At thirteen Gandhi is married to Kasturbai in a triple wedding with his brother and a cousin, arranged for the elders' convenience. His father is badly hurt when his coach overturns on the way to the wedding. Gandhi quickly assumes a husband's authority.

updates.gandhi: Married at 13 to Kasturbai, a girl the same age. Recalls the ceremony fondly but now condemns it.
updates.kasturba: Married to Gandhi at 13 in Porbandar. They are shy at first but gradually begin to talk freely.
updates.karamchand: Injured when his coach toppled over while hurrying from Rajkot to Porbandar for the wedding; attended bandaged.
updates.karsandas: Married in the same triple ceremony as Mohandas.
updates.laxmidas: Already married by the time of the triple wedding.
updates.tulsidas: Helped arrange the triple wedding; he and Karamchand were both old.
updates.childmarriage: Gandhi calls his marriage at 13 preposterous. It was arranged for economy and convenience, with no thought of the children.

status.gandhi: Age 13, newly married, at high school

chapters.situation: Gandhi, aged 13, has just been married to Kasturbai in a joint family wedding.
chapters.summary: Gandhi becomes a jealous, controlling husband who tries to restrict Kasturbai's movements. She defies him and goes wherever she likes. He is consumed by passion for her and tries without success to teach her to read. Long stays at her parents' home keep them apart much of the time.

updates.gandhi: A jealous husband who wants to 'make' his wife ideal. He keeps her up at night talking and cannot teach her to read.
updates.kasturba: Refuses to accept her husband's restrictions and goes to temples and friends as she pleases. Illiterate; spends much of these years at her parents' home.
updates.brahmacharya: Gandhi admits his love for Kasturbai was full of lust; only his sense of duty and truthfulness kept him from ruin.
updates.childmarriage: Gandhi notes that the custom of sending child-wives home to their parents softened the harm of early marriage.

status.kasturba: Child-wife in Rajkot, often at her parents' home

chapters.situation: Gandhi is a teenage husband, jealous and passionate, still at high school in Rajkot.
chapters.summary: Marriage costs Gandhi a year of school and ends his brother's studies. He wins scholarships and guards his reputation fiercely. He is wrongly fined for lying when a cloudy sky makes him late, and learns that truth requires care. A kind Sanskrit teacher keeps him in Sanskrit class.

updates.gandhi: Wins scholarships at high school and dreads any rebuke. Nurses his father after school. Struggles with English-medium geometry until it suddenly clicks.
updates.karsandas: Gave up studies altogether after the marriage.
updates.karamchand: Wrote to the headmaster asking that Mohandas be excused from gymnastics so he could come home and nurse him.
updates.gimi: Made gymnastics compulsory, refused Gandhi an exemption, and fined him for lateness he took as lying.
updates.pandya: Coaxed Gandhi back from the 'easy' Persian class to Sanskrit; Gandhi later thanks him for it.
updates.truth: Lesson from the wrongful fine: 'a man of truth must also be a man of care.'

status.gandhi: High-school student in Rajkot, nursing his father

chapters.situation: Gandhi is a dutiful high-school student who nurses his ailing father and prizes his good name.
chapters.summary: Gandhi befriends his elder brother's daring classmate in order to 'reform' him, against the warnings of his mother, brother and wife. The friend argues that meat makes the English strong. Gandhi, ashamed of his own fears of ghosts and the dark, agrees to try meat in secret.

updates.gandhi: Takes up an intimate friendship meant to reform the friend. Admits he is a coward, afraid of thieves, ghosts and snakes, and decides to eat meat in secret.
updates.mehtab: Introduced as a strong runner and jumper who claims meat-eating makes him fearless. Tells Gandhi that teachers and prominent men secretly eat meat.
updates.laxmidas: Warned Gandhi against the friend. Gandhi dared not openly defy him or their mother.
updates.karsandas: Has already secretly started eating meat and backs the friend's arguments.
updates.putlibai: Warned her son against bad company.
updates.kasturba: Warned her husband about the friend, but he was too proud to listen. She was braver than him and feared neither ghosts nor serpents.
updates.diet: A 'reform' craze in Rajkot claims meat will make Indians strong enough to defeat the English. Gandhi is persuaded.
updates.ahimsa: Gandhi later concludes that close friendships aimed at reform are dangerous, because vice spreads more easily than virtue.

chapters.situation: Persuaded by his friend that meat will make him strong, Gandhi has agreed to secretly try it despite his family's strict Vaishnava faith.
chapters.summary: Gandhi eats goat's meat by the river, feels sick, and dreams of a goat bleating inside him. About half a dozen secret meat feasts follow. He gives up meat because he cannot bear lying to his mother. The friend takes him to a brothel, where Gandhi freezes and is thrown out. The friend also stirs up his suspicions of Kasturbai.

updates.gandhi: Eats meat secretly for about a year, then vows to abstain while his parents live rather than keep lying. Narrowly escapes 'sin' at a brothel and later counts it a moral lapse anyway.
updates.mehtab: Arranges meat feasts at a State house and pays for them; takes Gandhi to a brothel; feeds Gandhi's jealousy with stories about Kasturbai.
updates.kasturba: Suffers her husband's jealous cruelty, fuelled by the friend's tales. Gandhi says he can never forgive himself for it.
updates.putlibai: Is lied to by her son ('no appetite today') during the meat-eating period; never learns the truth.
updates.diet: Gandhi's first meat makes him ill. He comes to like the dishes but gives them up to stop lying to his parents.
updates.brahmacharya: First of several narrow escapes from infidelity, saved, he says, by Providence rather than will.
updates.ahimsa: Gandhi says suspicion of his wife was rooted out only when he understood ahimsa and saw the wife as an equal partner.

status.gandhi: ~15, has given up meat but still under his friend's influence

chapters.situation: Gandhi has given up his secret meat-eating to stop lying to his parents, but remains close to the friend who led him into it.
chapters.summary: Gandhi confesses earlier faults. He and a relative smoked stolen cigarette stumps and tried suicide with datura seeds, then lost their nerve. At fifteen he clips gold from his brother's armlet to pay off a debt. He writes a confession to his bedridden father, who weeps silently and tears it up. Gandhi calls this his first lesson in ahimsa.

updates.gandhi: Gives up smoking after a botched suicide attempt. Steals gold for his brother, then confesses in writing to his father and vows never to steal again.
updates.karamchand: Bedridden with a fistula. Reads his son's written confession, weeps, tears up the note and forgives him without a word.
updates.karsandas: Ran up a debt of about 25 rupees; Mohandas clipped gold from his armlet to clear it.
updates.tulsidas: His smoking habit inspired the boys to pilfer his cigarette stumps.
updates.ahimsa: The father's silent forgiveness is Gandhi's 'object-lesson in Ahimsa': all-embracing love that transforms what it touches.
updates.truth: Gandhi learns the power of a clean confession joined to a promise never to repeat the wrong.

chapters.situation: Gandhi is 16. His father is bedridden with a fistula and Gandhi nurses him every evening, while Kasturbai is expecting their first child.
chapters.summary: Gandhi nurses his dying father but hurries to his wife's bed each night. On the fateful night his uncle relieves him, and the father dies minutes after Gandhi has gone to the bedroom. Gandhi calls this his 'double shame'. The baby born to Kasturbai lives only three or four days.

updates.gandhi: Misses his father's last moments because he left the sickroom for his wife. Carries the shame for life and calls himself 'a lustful, though a faithful, husband'.
updates.karamchand: Dies at Rajkot in 1885 after doctors disagree over an operation. Shortly before the end he writes 'Prepare for the last rites' and throws off his amulet.
updates.tulsidas: Sat with his dying brother and was at his side at the moment of death.
updates.kasturba: Gives birth to their first child, who survives only three or four days.
updates.putlibai: One of Karamchand's principal nurses in his final illness.
updates.brahmacharya: The 'double shame' of desire at the hour of his father's death becomes the root of Gandhi's later vow of brahmacharya.
